title: ice cream maker
text: ice cream maker. Ok... so you DO need to freeze the bowl at least 24 hours before making.  The booklet says it takes about 25 minutes to make a batch - but it is more like 45 minutes or more just to soft serve (And that is when you have REALLY cold ingredients and your bowl is properly frozen.) I used their booklet for the recipe too. Simple vanilla.  It was delicious - but I could have used 1/2 the sugar!  It was a bit too sweet for us.  Also, it was the non-cooked version - so no eggs.  If you use a cooked recipe it will be more custardy.. because it's cooked egg.  This machine is NOT timed it would run forever if you let it... it has a simple dial - on / off.  Nothing fancy at all.  However the price reflects this.  It's a fair price and pretty simple.  You need to hand wash the freezer bowl - and the paddle and the clear plastic lid... easy to do.  When I make some ice cream again- I am going to try 1/2 a recipe size and 1/2 the sugar and see how it goes.  If you don't want to spend hundreds of dollars and like a little homemade ice cream treat once in a while I think this machine is a good option.  Having said all of this, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

description: Housed in brushed stainless steel with an embossed logo, this fully automatic small appliance makes frozen yogurt, sorbet, and homemade ice cream in as little as 25 minutes. The frozen-dessert maker features a heavy-duty motor and a double-insulated freezer bowl that holds up to 2 quarts of frozen dessert at a time. Simply add ingredients, turn the machine on, and frozen drinks and desserts are ready in minutes. Its large ingredient spout allows for easily adding favorite mix-ins, and an instruction book and recipes come included. A fun addition to any birthday party or backyard barbecue, the frozen-dessert maker measures approximately 8-1/4 by 8 by 11-1/4 inches.
